title: Articles: a, an, the, zero
summary: Master when to use articles with countable and uncountable nouns — one of the most common band-limiters.

title: Present Perfect for IELTS
summary: Use present perfect for recent changes and life experience — essential for Writing Task 1 trends and Speaking.
example: The population has grown by 10% since 2010.

title: Conditionals: types 0–3
summary: First, second and third conditionals for hypothetical discussion — the backbone of Speaking Part 3.
example: If governments invested more, cities would become cleaner.

title: Passive voice in reports
summary: Report data objectively with the passive — a key feature of Academic Task 1.
example: The figures were collected over a ten-year period.

title: Relative clauses for detail
summary: Adding precise detail with who/which/where clauses lifts both writing and speaking quality.
example: Students who practise daily improve faster.

title: Complex sentences & subordination
summary: Although, despite, while, whereas — combine ideas like a fluent writer.
example: Although online learning is flexible, it cannot fully replace classrooms.

title: Nominalisation
summary: Turn verbs into nouns for a formal, academic tone.
example: The achievement of targets requires planning.

title: Inversion for emphasis
summary: Rarely have candidates mastered this — use inversion to stand out.
example: Not only is it cheap, but it is also effective.
